family: Bird and wildlife refuges and lighthouse reservations

mechanisms.description: An order that only revokes, restores, reduces or redescribes another reservation is spent on issue: its command is executed the day it is signed, and its effect is evidence for the other order's lifecycle.
An order that states its own end date or a fixed preference period ends by its own terms on that date.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: stated date, or order date plus the stated period

mechanisms.description: A later executive order whose held text revokes or supersedes the member in full ends it.
A later Public Land Order of the Secretary of the Interior revoking the member in full, identified by the official BLM Table of Public Land Orders, ends it.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: PLO signature date from the BLM table (the Federal Register publication may be a few days later)

mechanisms.description: Refuge System statute: an area in the National Wildlife Refuge System on or after January 1, 1975, including one designated by Executive order or included by public land withdrawal, stays in the System until an Act of Congress provides otherwise; the Secretary may not revoke withdrawals that added lands to the System before October 21, 1976.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: persistence from the date the area is shown in the System (no earlier than 1975-01-01) to the cutoff

mechanisms.description: Statutes and a regulation in force on the cutoff that name the member or its refuge and keep its reservation in operation (Pub. L. 100-226 sec. 3; 50 CFR 216.85; 43 U.S.C. 1787(b)(4); ANILCA secs. 303 and 305).

Transfers of administration and renaming (Biological Survey to Interior and Lighthouses to the Coast Guard in 1939; renaming as National Wildlife Refuges in 1940), the FLPMA savings clause and the repeal of withdrawal authority continue the reservations and never end them.

Station-by-station disposal of light stations (surplus property, National Historic Lighthouse Preservation Act) and the FLPMA withdrawal review end a reservation only through a PLO or deed that names it.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: date of the PLO or deed, when found

mechanisms.description: Lands acquired under the Migratory Bird Conservation Act are federal by title; the order reserves them, and their disposal needs Migratory Bird Conservation Commission approval.

procedure.description: Pribilof Reservation, Walrus and Otter Islands (EO 1044), named in a current regulation.

when.text_regex: Walrus island and Otter island|Walrus and Otter

lead.basis: 50 CFR 216.85, in force on 2026-10-14, states that EO 1044 set aside Walrus and Otter Islands as bird reservations and prohibits landing on them except as authorized; ANILCA sec. 303(1) includes the existing Pribilof (Walrus and Otter Islands) refuge in the Alaska Maritime NWR and sec. 305 keeps the Executive orders for Alaska refuge units in force.

gaps: Only the eCFR search excerpt and section text line of 50 CFR 216.85 are held (current-law MENTIONS.csv); the full section should be retained.

procedure.description: Jupiter Inlet lighthouse reservation adjustment (EO 4254), named by a current statute as an existing withdrawal.

lead.basis: 43 U.S.C. 1787(b)(4) (2008, in the current U.S. Code) makes the Jupiter Inlet withdrawal subject to "any existing withdrawals under the Executive orders" it lists, including "Executive Order No. 4254 (June 12, 1925)"; PLO 7202 (1996) revoked EO 4254 only in part.

gaps: The phrase treating the EO 4254 withdrawal as existing (subsec. (b)(4)(A)) is read on the web; only the listing in (b)(4)(B) is held.
PLO 7202 (61 FR 29758), which revoked EO 4254 in part in 1996, is known only from the held BLM table; the lands it left withdrawn are not identified in a held copy.

procedure.description: Alaska bird reservations that ANILCA sec. 303 names as existing refuges and sec. 305 keeps in force: Bering Sea (1037), Tuxedni (1039), Saint Lazaria (1040), Bogoslof (1049), Forrester Island (1458), Hazy Islands (1459), Chamisso Island (1658), Nunivak (5095, 5470) and the Amak Island addition to the Aleutian Islands Reservation (5318).

lead.basis: ANILCA sec. 305 provides that "All proclamations, Executive orders, public land orders, and other administrative actions in effect on the day before the date of the enactment of this Act with respect to units of the National Wildlife Refuge System in the State shall remain in force and effect" except where inconsistent with ANILCA or ANCSA, and that land within the boundaries of any such action is included in the refuge into which sec. 303 incorporates the unit; sec. 303 incorporates "the existing" Bering Sea, Tuxedni, Saint Lazaria, Bogoslof, Forrester Island, Hazy Islands, Chamisso and Aleutian Islands refuges into the Alaska Maritime NWR and the existing Nunivak refuge into the Yukon Delta NWR; 16 U.S.C. 668dd(a)(6) keeps those areas in the System until Congress acts. The member maps to its sec. 303 refuge through its own words and a held instrument: eight orders name their reservation ("This reservation to be known as Bering Sea Reservation"; EO 5318 and 5470 add lands "to ... the Aleutian Islands Reservation" and "the Nunivak Island Reservation"), and Proclamation 2416 (held) renamed each of those reservations as the National Wildlife Refuge of the name sec. 303 uses. EO 5095 does not name its reservation; it is linked to the Nunivak Island Reservation of Proclamation 2416 only by the island name.

gaps: ANILCA (secs. 303 and 305) is read on the web (NPS electronic version), not held; these yes leads wait on its acquisition, and sec. 305's Statutes at Large page is taken from that version.

Sec. 305 reaches the member as an Executive order in effect on December 1, 1980 for an Alaska refuge unit; that the order was still in effect on that date is inferred from sec. 303's naming the refuge as existing, not from a record naming the order.
EO 5095: the link to the Nunivak Island Reservation and Nunivak NWR rests on the island name alone; the order itself gives no reservation name.
Parts may have been conveyed under ANCSA or revoked in part (EO 1039 in part by PLO 484, 1948; EO 5095 in part by PLO 1177, 1955); a partial end leaves the order in force as amended.

procedure.description: EO 4490: revokes EO 1763 and opens the lands for a 91-day ex-service preference beginning on the 63rd day; spent when that period ran out.

lead.basis: The revocation was executed on signature; the only continuing command, the 91-day preference period beginning on the 63rd day after August 3, 1926, ran out by its own terms by January 3, 1927.

date_rule.basis: order date to the end of the stated 91-day period

gaps: The preference period restricts entry for a stated time only; after it the lands pass to the general public land laws, so no reversion, retained tract or lasting purpose restriction remains.

procedure.description: EO 5000: revokes EO 1733 as to six Aleutian islands and opens them for a 91-day ex-service preference beginning on the 63rd day; spent when that period ran out.

date_rule.basis: order date to the end of the stated 91-day period

gaps: The preference period restricts entry for a stated time only; after it the lands pass to the public land laws subject to existing withdrawals.

procedure.description: Orders whose only operative content revokes another reservation, restores land, or reduces a reservation by excluding land (P1).

lead.basis: The order's own text shows one operative act, a revocation, restoration or reduction of another reservation, executed on its date; the consequence belongs to the other order's lifecycle and the land's history (coordinator ruling P1).

gaps: None of these orders adds land, keeps a reversion, retains a tract, reserves a right or restricts the restored land's use; orders that add land (enlargements, mixed boundary changes) are excluded and stay open.

Held later edges on EO 2872 (EO 3964, 1924; EO 5747, 1931) modify the parent Big Lake Reservation of EO 2230, which they cite together with EO 2872; they are events of the parent, not acts on this spent order.

procedure.description: Orders whose only operative content amends another order without adding land: EO 5458 redescribes the EO 4410 lighthouse tract by official survey; EO 5457 amends restoration order EO 5243 to revoke a 1901 withdrawal and to exclude reserved lighthouse and naval lands from the restoration (P2).

lead.basis: The order's own text shows that amending another order is its only operative content; under the strike-and-insert ruling its text merges into the parent on issue (coordinator ruling P2). Its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it.

gaps: Its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it (EO 4410 was revoked in part by PLO 7165, 1995; EO 5243 is not a member of this family).
If the owner treats an amending order as living as long as the amended text lives, these leads become open pending the parent.

procedure.description: Members misclassified into this family, named with the family that should decide them: EO 1485 (Indian-reservation restoration; PD-INDIAN), EO 2012 (relief of Americans abroad, 1914; PD-WAR-EMERGENCY), EO 3036 (civil service schedule; PD-CS-RULES), EO 2670 (Virgin Islands lighthouse administration; PD-ADMIN), EO 6724 and EO 7345 (fund and acquisition authorizations; PD-ADMIN), EO 3237 (Canal Zone naval radio site; PD-CLASS-EVENTS, canal_zone).

lead.basis: The member's own text shows the order is not a refuge or lighthouse reservation; it stays open here and should be decided under the doctrine named for it.

gaps: Route to PD-INDIAN (1485), PD-WAR-EMERGENCY or PD-ADMIN (2012, 2670, 6724, 7345), PD-CS-RULES (3036), PD-CLASS-EVENTS canal_zone (3237).

procedure.description: Blackbeard Island chain: EO 1993 (reservation, 1914) was vacated by EO 2203 (1915) and restored by EO 3957 (1924); EO 2203 also gave a standing direction against hunting permits.

lead.basis: EO 3957 (held) restores the 1914 reservation "in its original area and for the original purpose"; whether that revives EO 1993 or reserves anew, and whether it revokes EO 2203 (the verb is illegible in the held OCR), is not established.

gaps: A legible copy of EO 3957 (Federal Register did not yet exist; National Archives or the 1924 State Department slip) is needed.
Blackbeard Island National Wildlife Refuge exists today, but no held record ties it to EO 1993 rather than EO 3957.

procedure.description: Temporary withdrawals (pending legislation, classification, selection, or "temporarily withdrawn" for refuge or lighthouse use) with no held revocation.

when.any_regex: (be|hereby,?) temporarily with-? ?drawn|Temporarily Withdrawing|withdrawn for classification|for classification as to|in aid of (pending )?legislation|pending (determination|legislation|classification)|for possible use

lead.basis: A withdrawal "pending" a purpose does not end when the purpose is met or abandoned; it ends only when revoked. No held order or PLO revokes this member in full, and the FLPMA savings clause continues withdrawals in existence in 1976.

gaps: Search the BLM PLO tables and the Federal Register for a PLO naming the order by number or date (several members of this kind were revoked by PLOs; partial revocations, such as EO 4939 by PLO 121, 1943, do not end the order).
A temporary withdrawal later absorbed into a refuge reservation of the same lands is superseded in fact but stays open unless an order says so.

procedure.description: Refuge reservations reserving lands "acquired or to be acquired" under the Migratory Bird Conservation Act, with no held revocation.

when.text_regex: acquired or to be acquired|acquired by the United States

lead.basis: If the refuge was in the National Wildlife Refuge System on or after January 1, 1975, 16 U.S.C. 668dd(a)(6) keeps it there until Congress acts, and acquired refuge lands may be disposed of only with Migratory Bird Conservation Commission approval; no held current record ties this order to a current refuge unit.

gaps: Needed: a reviewed crosswalk from each order to a current refuge unit in the FWS Annual Report of Lands (FY2024 Table 3 lists refuge names and acreage, not executive orders) or the refuge's FWS establishing-document file.
No held search shows a full revocation; absence of a found revocation is not evidence of persistence.

procedure.description: Other bird and wildlife refuge reservations (establishments, re-establishments, enlargements, transfers for refuge use) with no held full revocation.

lead.basis: A refuge reservation continues until revoked; renaming (1940) and transfer to Interior (1939) continue it; if the area was in the Refuge System on or after January 1, 1975, 16 U.S.C. 668dd(a)(6) and 43 U.S.C. 1714(j) keep it until Congress acts. Whether the order's lands were still reserved in 1975 is not shown by the fields held.

gaps: Needed: evidence that the order's area was in the Refuge System on or after 1975-01-01 (FWS Annual Report of Lands for 1975 and the current year, matched to the order by a reviewed crosswalk) or a PLO revoking it.

Several such orders were revoked in part by PLOs (EO 2446 by PLO 2291, EO 4519 by PLO 988, EO 7106 by PLO 4641 and amended by PLO 1511, EO 7489 by PLO 3385); a partial revocation leaves the order in force as amended.
Wikisource notes are leads only: EO 779 (Tortugas Keys) 'revoked by Proclamation 2112, January 4, 1935' is not verified in a held source.

procedure.description: Lighthouse reservations and transfers of land for lighthouse purposes with no held full revocation.

lead.basis: A lighthouse reservation continues until revoked by order or PLO, or until the station is conveyed; the 1939 transfer of the Bureau of Lighthouses to the Coast Guard and transfers of jurisdiction (for example EO 6896 moving San Miguel and Prince Islands to the Navy) continue it. Many such reservations were revoked by PLOs after 1947, station by station; none is held for this member.

gaps: Held later edges flagged by the engine are not full ends: PLO 1724 (1958) revokes EO 431 ("EOs of ... Mar. 27, 1906") only "in part" per the BLM table; PLO 7391 (1999) revokes an Oregon power-site order of November 14, 1917, a date collision with EO 2755, not EO 2755 itself.

Search the BLM PLO tables (held) and Federal Register for a PLO naming the order by number or date; the 1867-1906 and Alaska multi-site orders (for example EO 4257, revoked in part by six PLOs 1960-1994) need site-by-site review.
Light stations conveyed under the National Historic Lighthouse Preservation Act (2000) or surplus-property law end by deed; GSA and NPS conveyance lists are not held.

procedure.description: Catch-all.

lead.basis: No branch applies; the member needs individual review.

gaps: No rule of this doctrine reaches this member.

undecidable.reason: Refuge reservations with no held revocation and no held current record tying the order to a current refuge unit; decidable once a reviewed order-to-refuge crosswalk against the FWS Annual Report of Lands (and the 1975 edition) exists.
Lighthouse reservations with no held full revocation; decidable by a PLO or deed naming the order.
Temporary withdrawals with no held revocation.
Blackbeard Island chain with an illegible revoking verb.
Members whose held text shows another type.
